data.description:
## Goal

**As an** operator, **I want** a measured verdict on the two chain/routing fixes shipped on 2026-11-03, **so that** "it is fixed" is a claim backed by a like-for-like before/after comparison against the configuration's own scheduled windows — not by the absence of complaints.

**Earliest implementation time: 2026-11-04 04:00 UTC.** That is the end of the first remote-closed window (`01:00-04:00` UTC) that completes after the 2026-11-03 14:25:10 UTC restart, so it is the first instant with (a) ≥13.5 h of post-fix log and (b) a full scheduled-gap sample. See **Timing** for why 2026-11-04 10:00 UTC is the *preferred* like-for-like point.

discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK, discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5.

## What is deployed

| Item | Commit | What it should change |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK — fail fast on a provably dead chain | `7892d22d` | no chain hold when every provider is deterministically skipped or terminally refused; earliest-reset `Retry-After`; a `remote-ok` request is never bounced onto a chain with no capacity |
| LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 — diagnosable lease occupancy | `763ed61f` | `local_dispatch_denied` carries the full occupancy evidence; `local_occupancy_divergence` names contradictions; stale records cannot block |

Deployed by restart **2026-11-03 14:25:09–14:25:10 UTC** (proxy pid 158427; `llama-server` and TTS relaunched and all three healthy). **The post-fix measurement window starts at 2026-11-03 14:25:10 UTC** (log rotation line `14:25:10,847 - INFO - Rotated previous proxy log`). Anything before that line is pre-fix.

## Timing: when the fix can actually fire

`model=code` has 7 providers; the gates that create a *provably dead* chain are the `available_times` windows:

| Provider | `available_times` (UTC) | Closed |
|---|---|---|
| `local-qwen3` | unrestricted | — |
| `munitoai-free` | unrestricted | gated only by usage-limit reset / quota |
| `opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go-3` | `00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00` | **01:00–04:00**, **06:00–10:00** |
| `deepseek-flash` | `00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00` | **01:00–04:00**, **06:00–10:00** |
| `munitoai` | `10:00-23:00` | **23:00–10:00** |

So the chain is *window*-dead only in **01:00–04:00** and **06:00–10:00** UTC, and it is only *provably* dead when `munitoai-free` is also out (usage-limit reset / quota) — which is exactly the 2026-11-03 08:41 shape. `munitoai-free`'s recorded reset was `2026-11-04T00:02Z`, so **the 01:00–04:00 gap on 2026-11-04 may legitimately have a live provider and therefore no trigger**; that is correct behaviour, not evidence of anything.

Therefore:

- **earliest defensible evaluation:** 2026-11-04 **04:00 UTC** (first complete post-fix gap);
- **preferred like-for-like evaluation:** 2026-11-04 **10:00 UTC**, i.e. the end of the `06:00–10:00` gap — the same clock window as the baseline below;
- if neither gap produced a trigger, conclude **inconclusive** (say so explicitly) and re-check at the next gap or at the next usage-limit/quota block rather than recording a fake pass.

## Baseline (pre-fix)

Recorded evidence, for the record:

- 2026-11-03 **08:41:42** — every remote provider deterministically skipped (`munitoai-free` `usage_limit_reset_pending` reset ~15.4 h away; `opencode-go-3` `quota_exhausted` ~14 days; four entries `outside_available_window`) and the proxy logged `Chain exhausted ... holding 300s before restarting cycle` **three times**. The audit subprocess (`audit-RISE-0MVZEOVQG0075XSU-...`) received a 429 in 0.4 s and could never succeed; its 1080 s per-call screen budget was consumed by holds.
- 2026-11-03 **08:40:05** — `Returning first provider error response instead of generic exhausted message ... (status=400)` followed immediately by two 300 s holds (the first provider's raw 400 carried no `Retry-After`, which is what re-enabled the "legacy full hold").
- 2026-11-03 **08:49:40** — local guard refused with `eta_prefill_s=45.2 enforced=true` and the request was routed onto the dead remote chain (`outcome=exhausted`); **08:50:41** the identical prompt and identical ETA were admitted (`enforced=false`, `eta_occupancy_s=0.0`) and produced a first byte in 6 s.
- 2026-11-03 **08:49:31.690** — `local_dispatch_denied session=... owner=... active=1` on a two-slot pool while `/llama/local/status` at 08:49:31.034 reported `available_slots=2`: the refusal named an owner and a count but not which gate refused.

### Measured baseline — log file `proxy.log.2026-11-03_101625`, window 08:37:26 → 10:16:25 UTC (99 min)

This is the pre-fix window captured by the log rotated at the 10:16 restart. It sits inside the `06:00–10:00` closed gap, i.e. it is the like-for-like comparison window.

| Signal | Count (99 min) |
|---|---|
| `Chain exhausted for model=` (holds taken) | **105** — 36 of them `holding 300s`, plus 30 s / 120 s / 38 s / 17 s variants |
| `All providers exhausted for model=` | 189 |
| deterministic-skip vocabulary | `usage_limit_reset_pending` 1198 · `outside its available_times window` 884 · `quota_exhausted` 1230 |
| `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` | 137 |
| … of which `reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` | **57** (11 distinct sessions) |
| `local_dispatch_denied` | 26 (none carrying occupancy evidence) |

### Control window — open windows, no trigger expected

`proxy.log`, 10:16:29 → 13:34:50 UTC (3 h 18 m; remote windows **open** that whole time): `Chain exhausted` **0**, `All providers exhausted` **0**, `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` 334 (46 × `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` — correct fall-throughs, because remote had capacity), `local_dispatch_denied` 97. Use this as the "no trigger + open chain" reference: it shows what a *healthy* zero looks like, and it is why "0 holds" alone proves nothing.

Log retention is 7 days (`Pruned old rotated log ... > 7 days old`), so the baseline file survives until ~2026-11-10. Re-extract the numbers above if it is needed after that; do not assume it is still there.

## Measurement technique

Rules that keep the comparison honest:

1. **Like-for-like windows only.** Compare post-fix samples taken inside a *closed* window (`01:00–04:00` / `06:00–10:00` UTC) against the baseline above. Never compare an open-window sample against it; an open chain cannot trigger the fix, so it will always look "fixed".
2. **Normalise per hour** — sample lengths will differ; report counts per hour as well as raw counts.
3. **Check chain aliveness before interpreting a zero.** If no trigger fired, prove the chain was actually provably dead in that window (`munitoai-free` unavailable *and* the four window-gated providers closed). A zero with a live chain is `inconclusive`, not `fixed`.
4. **Exclude the restart verification probe** from the sample: session `verify-lp-0mw0kzr7a003ufqk-restart` (2026-11-03 14:25:54, 18/8/26 tokens) exists only to prove the deploy.
5. **Quote the log line, not the count**, for anything that decides the verdict — a count can be satisfied by a wrong reason.

### LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK (fail fast / no bounce) — expected post-fix signatures

```bash
LOG=/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log            # or the rotated file covering the chosen window
# 1. the fail-fast line replaces the hold, on one vocabulary
grep -c 'chain_planned_unavailable'          $LOG    # expect > 0 in a provably-dead window
grep -m3 'chain_planned_unavailable'         $LOG    # inspect reason=, hold=skipped, retry_after=, deterministic_skips=, terminal=
# 2. no hold on a provably dead chain
grep -c 'Chain exhausted for model='         $LOG    # expect 0 in that window (baseline: 105/99 min)
# 3. the local override instead of a bounce onto a dead chain
grep -c 'local_admission_guard_local_wait'   $LOG    # expect > 0 where the old code emitted direct_fallback
grep 'local_admission_guard_direct_fallback' $LOG | grep -c 'reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct'   # expect 0 *while the chain is dead* (baseline 57)
# 4. retry timing is honest (earliest reset, body == header, capped)
grep 'chain_planned_unavailable' $LOG | grep -o 'retry_after=[0-9]*' | sort -u
# 5. the client-visible shape (the preserved first error, now timed)
grep 'Returning first provider error response' $LOG | tail -3
# 6. the report renders the new section
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24   # "## Chain-end outcomes"
```

Targets:

| Metric | Baseline | Target |
|---|---|---|
| `Chain exhausted` (holds) per closed-window hour | 105 / 1.65 h ≈ **64/h** | **0** where every skip is deterministic; unchanged for transient chains (cooldown / 5xx / connection error) — verify at least one transient hold still occurs |
| `chain_planned_unavailable ... hold=skipped` | 0 (line did not exist) | > 0, one per affected request (not per provider) |
| `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` with a dead chain | 57 / 99 min | **0**, replaced by `local_admission_guard_local_wait` |
| `All providers exhausted` reached from a local ETA refusal | the 08:49:40 shape | **0** |
| audit-* call latency on a doomed chain | 300 s × 3 holds before the error | < 1 s |
| Advertised `retry_after` | cap-derived (3600) or absent | the earliest known reset, capped by `max_retry_after_seconds`, equal to the `Retry-After` header |

Per-line acceptance (AC2/AC4 of the item):
- `local_admission_guard_local_wait` must appear **with** `reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` and **without** a following `→ routing to next provider` line;
- `chain_planned_unavailable` must **not** appear in a window where a provider was merely cooling down (that would be a false positive — the verdict must stay conservative).

### LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 (diagnostics) — this half is measurable within hours

Denials happen under local contention (26 in 99 min pre-fix; 97 in 3 h 18 m), so this verdict does not need a closed window:

```bash
LOG=/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
# every denial must carry the evidence suffix (fields: records_total, records_active,
# records_unexpired, records_stale, active_counter, max_local, generating,
# prefill_in_flight, prefill_cap, llama_available_slots, llama_total_slots, records=…)
grep -c 'local_dispatch_denied'                                  $LOG
grep -c 'local_dispatch_denied.*records_total='                  $LOG    # expect == the count above
# contradictions are logged, and the "our own numbers cannot explain it" class must be zero
grep -c 'local_occupancy_divergence reason=llama_reports_free_slots'  $LOG   # > 0 is fine (prefill cap vs llama view)
grep -c 'local_occupancy_divergence reason=occupancy_unexplained'     $LOG   # must be 0 — non-zero is a bookkeeping defect, file it
# which cap refused is now readable without a repro
grep -m3 'local_dispatch_denied' $LOG | grep -o 'generating=[0-9]*\|prefill_in_flight=[0-9]*\|prefill_cap=[0-9]*\|max_local=[0-9]*'
```

Targets: 100 % of `local_dispatch_denied` lines carry the evidence; `occupancy_unexplained` **0**; the 08:49:31 question ("denied with `available_slots=2` — which gate?") answerable from the line alone (expect `prefill_in_flight=1 prefill_cap=1`, i.e. the serialised-prefill cap, for that shape).

## Decision criteria

| Outcome | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **fixed** | a provably-dead window shows ≥1 `chain_planned_unavailable ... hold=skipped`, **0** holds, and the evidence suffix on every denial | close with the numbers; no follow-up |
| **partial** | fail-fast fires but a hold still occurs on a deterministic chain, or a denial lacks the evidence suffix | file a `test-failure`/bug item naming the exact line and reason; do not close |
| **not fixed** | a provably-dead window still shows `Chain exhausted` / `direct_fallback`, and no `chain_planned_unavailable` | reopen LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK (or file a new bug) with the window and the log lines |
| **inconclusive** | no provably-dead window occurred in the sample | record it, keep the item open, re-check at the next gap/usage-limit block; never record a pass |
| **regression** | holds disappear on *transient* chains too (cooldown/5xx), or `occupancy_unexplained` > 0 | treat as a defect: the verdict is over-firing |

If any outcome requires code change, create the follow-up item (`discovered-from:<this id>`) and implement it in its own worktree — this item is measurement only.

## Out of scope

- Changing provider `available_times` or adding an always-on remote provider (the operator rejected that on 2026-10-31; see LP-0MVWC9CZH004OZYN).
- Extending the classifier or the `chain_planned_unavailable` vocabulary — that is now owned by epic LP-0MVWC9CZH004OZYN (its AC11, extend-never-fork).
- Re-litigating the incident's per-call budget arithmetic.

## Candidate follow-up observed during the restart (not measured here)

Before the 2026-11-03 14:25 restart, `/llama/local/status` reported `llama_server_running=true`, `available_slots=2/2`, `capacity_hint=idle` for ~3 hours while **no `llama-server` process existed** (`llama-server.log` ends `start-llama.sh: line 273: 4168 Killed` at 11:33) and local dispatches were failing with `ConnectError`. `/health` said `healthy` throughout. That is a stale *running-state* divergence (distinct from the slot-count divergence fixed in LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5): file it separately with this evidence if it reproduces — it is a candidate for the same "engine view vs route view" family.

## Assumptions

- The deployed code is what runs: proxy started 14:25:09 UTC, `dev` HEAD `7892d22d` committed 12:54 — confirm again at evaluation time with `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>` and `git log -1 --format=%cI dev`.

## Goal

**As an** operator reading the after-acceptance eviction signal, **I want** a local dispatch that **completed successfully** to be released without being reported as `local_eviction_after_acceptance`, **so that** the AC7(a) defect detector (LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S) counts real evictions instead of ordinary lease expiry.

## Evidence (2026-11-03 14:25:54 → 14:26:34 UTC, `dev` `7892d22d`)

A small verification request that **succeeded in 0.57 s** was 40 s later reported as an eviction after acceptance:

```
14:25:54  routing_check provider=local-qwen3 ... estimated_tokens=8
14:25:54  [local] POST ...  Stream finished: reason=length tokens=18/8/26 stream=false
14:25:54  lease_renewed session=verify-... timeout=30s
14:25:54  local_preference_resolved preference=remote-ok outcome=local reason=none
14:26:34  local_eviction     ... reason=slot_assignment_freed slot=0
14:26:34  local_eviction_after_acceptance ... reason=idle_timeout estimated_tokens=8
          new_tokens=8 eta_prefill_s=0.0 elapsed_s=40.1
14:26:34  lease_released session=verify-... reason=idle_timeout
```

Three things are wrong together:

1. `local_eviction_after_acceptance` is documented as "accepted local dispatches evicted **before their first byte**" — this request produced its first byte (and its last) within 0.57 s, so it was never evicted *after acceptance* in the intended sense;
2. `elapsed_s=40.1` is the *lease's* idle lifetime (30 s timeout + slack), not the request duration — so the field mixes two different clocks;
3. the event is emitted on the routine `lease_released ... reason=idle_timeout` path, which is the normal way every completed local dispatch's record expires.

Measured frequency in this window: 7 `local_eviction` lines, 6 `reason=slot_assignment_freed` (expected churn) and 1 `reason=idle_timeout` — i.e. 100 % of the `idle_timeout` eviction reports in the sample are false positives, and the true-positive rate of the signal cannot be established while that is the case.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The `local_eviction_after_acceptance` event is emitted only when a dispatch was admitted and did **not** reach its first byte (the documented meaning); a completed or cancelled-after-first-byte dispatch releases silently or under its own reason.
- AC2: `elapsed_s` measures the request's own lifetime (admission → release), not the lease timeout, so the value agrees with the request's observed duration.
- AC3: A regression test drives the pattern above — one local dispatch that completes, then the idle lease release — and asserts **no** `local_eviction_after_acceptance` line; a second test drives a genuine admitted-then-never-first-byte dispatch and asserts the line **is** emitted with a truthful `elapsed_s`.
- AC4: Existing consumers keep working: `local_eviction_after_acceptance` stays a distinct event from `local_eviction`, its `reason` vocabulary is unchanged, and the usage-analysis report's after-acceptance breakdown (which splits by reason) still renders.
- AC5: Documentation of the event's meaning in `proxy/docs/routing.md` matches the behaviour.

## Out of scope

- The eviction reasons themselves (`measured_cache_deficit`, `prefill_deadline`, `idle_timeout`) and their thresholds.
- Any change to how leases are released — only to what is *reported* about the release.

## Key files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` — the `local_eviction` / `local_eviction_after_acceptance` emitters.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the idle-timeout / slot-assignment-free release paths and the dispatcher that records the event.
- `proxy/tests/` — `test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`, `test_lease_truthfulness.py`, and the usage-analysis `test_post_acceptance_eviction_report.py` contract.

## Assumptions

- The `slot_assignment_freed` line emitted immediately before it is the expected churn line and is not part of the defect.
- The window's single occurrence is representative of the routine path (every completed local dispatch leaves a record that later expires by `idle_timeout`), not a one-off; AC1/AC3 make that checkable rather than assumed.

## Provenance

# Launch authority: detect a foreign backend and refuse to spawn

**Parent:** LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 · **Type:** feature · **Phase 2 of 8**

## Context

`_try_adopt_running_llama_server()` decides ownership from
`proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` alone, and `start_llama_server()` spawns
unconditionally. When a container started outside the lifecycle holds port 8080
the proxy therefore adopts a server it did not start, then spawns doomed
host-side processes against the busy port (six `<defunct> llama-server` entries
on 2026-11-04).

## Change

Introduce a single authority check that inspects the **live** listener before
any adopt-or-spawn decision:

- New module `proxy/proxy/launch_authority.py` exposing
  `inspect_running_backend(srv) -> BackendInspection` with fields
  `present`, `pids`, `container` (name or `None`), `parallel`, `slot_save_path`,
  `lifecycle_owned`, `source` (`"absent" | "lifecycle" | "foreign"`).
- Reuse the existing, already container-aware helpers rather than duplicating
  them: `proxy.backend_rss.discover_llama_pids`, `_cmdline`,
  `container_name`, `container_init_pid`, and `lifecycle._find_pid_on_port`.
  Read the effective flags from the process `cmdline` (works for host and
  container: the container shares the host pid namespace).
- Wire the check into `_startup_launch_default_model_loader()` (and the
  on-demand `ensure_model_loaded()` spawn path) *before* adoption or spawn.
- On `source == "foreign"`: log one ERROR naming port, pid/container, resolved
  slot count and live `--parallel`, set a sticky `local_backend_foreign` flag,
  refuse local dispatch, and return without calling
  `subprocess.Popen`/`podman` — never leave defunct children.
- Surface the verdict in `/health` (`llama_backend_source`,
  `llama_backend_container`) and `/llama/local/status`.

## Policy decision (confirmed by the producer, 2026-11-05)

**Refuse and report.** A backend the lifecycle did not start is never adopted
and never taken over: the proxy refuses to spawn, reports the mismatch (port,
pid/container, resolved slot count, live `--parallel`) and leaves the running
process untouched, so an operator decides what to do with it. Taking ownership
is explicitly out of scope — stopping a working backend on a detection error is
a worse failure than reporting it.

Ownership is proven by (a) the tracked `llama_process` handle this proxy
spawned, or (b) a matching recorded signature **plus** a live process whose
`--parallel` and launch flags agree with the config. A signature match alone is
no longer sufficient — that is the gap this item closes. The proxy keeps
serving remote providers; the local tier fails closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Startup detects a llama-server the lifecycle did not start (host or container) and reports it explicitly, including the port, pid/container and the resolved slot count.
- [ ] No defunct host-side `llama-server` processes are produced when a container holds the port (test drives the lifecycle with the port pre-occupied).
- [ ] A signature match alone never yields `lifecycle_owned`; the live process flags must also agree.
- [ ] `/health` and `/llama/local/status` expose the backend source and, for a container holder, its name.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `inspect_running_backend()`: discover pids → read `cmdline` → parse
   `--parallel`/`-np` and `--slot-save-path` → resolve container via
   `backend_rss.container_name` → classify ownership.
2. Guard both spawn call sites with the inspection result.
3. Extend the health/status payload builders (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`).
4. Document the behaviour in `docs/dev/proxy-log-lifecycle.md` (lifecycle
   section) or a new `docs/dev/llama-launch-authority.md`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/launch_authority.py` (new)
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`
- `proxy/proxy/backend_rss.py` (reuse, no behaviour change)
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `docs/dev/llama-launch-authority.md` (new)

## Dependencies

Blocked by the test item (Phase 1) so the red baseline exists first.
data.title: Launch authority: detect a foreign backend and refuse to spawn

# Assert live `--parallel` against `session_slot_pool_size`

**Parent:** LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 · **Type:** feature · **Phase 3 of 8**

## Context

`models.ini` documents the constraint, `proxy/config.yaml` repeats it ("Keeping
these values aligned is critical"), and `lifecycle.start_llama_server()` does
export `LLAMA_PARALLEL` from `server.session_slot_pool_size` (LP-0MQMH0WHY005UPFA).
Nothing *enforces* it. A launch outside the lifecycle falls back to
`start-llama.sh`'s `: "${LLAMA_PARALLEL:=1}"`, producing a 1-slot server while
the proxy believes it has 2 — slot exhaustion and restore failures at runtime,
with no error anywhere.

## Change

1. **Proxy side:** extend `proxy/proxy/launch_authority.py` to expose the live
   `--parallel` (from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`; `--parallel N` for the router and
   `-np N`/`--parallel N` for a single-model server). At startup, after the
   backend reports ready, assert it equals `server.session_slot_pool_size`.
2. **Fail, do not warn:** on mismatch, log one ERROR naming both values, the
   live pid and the port; set a sticky `local_backend_parallel_mismatch` flag
   that refuses local dispatch, and fail the backend startup phase (the same
   path that already raises `RuntimeError` for an unready backend). The proxy
   keeps serving remote providers — see the policy note below.
3. **Start script:** replace the silent default in `./start-llama.sh` (both the
   router branch and the model branch) with a fail-fast: when `LLAMA_PARALLEL`
   is unset, print a FATAL message explaining that the proxy lifecycle is the
   only launch authority and exit non-zero (documented escape hatch
   `LLAMA_PARALLEL_DEFAULT_OK=1` for deliberate manual debugging).
4. Policy knob `server.llama_parallel_mismatch_policy: fail_local | abort`,
   **default `fail_local`** (producer-confirmed 2026-11-05): `fail_local` fails
   the local tier and keeps the proxy up for remote routing; `abort` refuses
   proxy startup and is available only as an operator opt-in. There is no
   `adopt` value: adopting a server whose slot geometry contradicts the
   configured pool cannot be made correct at runtime, so it is never offered.

## Policy note (confirmed by the producer, 2026-11-05)

AC1's "startup fails (not warns)" is implemented at the **local-backend** tier:
fatal for local dispatch, `/health` reports an error, one ERROR log line — and
the proxy keeps serving remote providers. Aborting the whole proxy on a foreign
container would have taken remote routing down too, the exact availability loss
the incident exposed, so `abort` stays an explicit opt-in rather than the
default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Startup fails (not warns) when the running llama-server's `--parallel` differs from `server.session_slot_pool_size`; test covers both the matching and mismatching cases.
- [ ] The mismatch ERROR line names the live `--parallel` value, the configured `session_slot_pool_size`, the backend pid and the port.
- [ ] `./start-llama.sh` refuses to launch when `LLAMA_PARALLEL` is unset, with an actionable message and a non-zero exit; the router and single-model branches are both covered by a test.
- [ ] The matched case is silent (no new warning) and leaves local dispatch enabled.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `launch_authority.parallel_mismatch(inspection, config) -> str | None`
   (pure function, unit-testable without processes).
2. Startup assertion + sticky flag + health field.
3. Two-line `start-llama.sh` guard per branch, plus a bash test in
   `tests/` (or `proxy/tests/`) that runs the script with a stubbed
   `LLAMA_SERVER_BIN` and asserts the exit code and message.
4. Config key + documentation in `proxy/config.yaml` next to
   `session_slot_pool_size`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/launch_authority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`
- `./start-llama.sh`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_launch_authority.py`

## Dependencies

Blocked by Phase 1 (tests) and Phase 2 (the inspection module this extends).
data.title: Assert live --parallel against session_slot_pool_size

# Log-path liveness check with container-aware resolution

**Parent:** LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 · **Type:** feature · **Phase 5 of 8**

## Context

After the 00:26 kill on 2026-11-04, `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`
received nothing for eight hours: the containerised server wrote its log
*inside* the container, so every llama-server file in the 24 h report was
`skipped_outside_window` and the report's Decode speed / Prompt eval speed /
Engine cross-check sections silently carried no source. The proxy had
`llama_log_age_seconds`, but nothing acted on it.

## Change

1. `ensure_log_liveness(srv, window_seconds=...)` in `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`:
   capture the watched log's size/mtime, wait a bounded window (default 90 s,
   config `server.llama_log_liveness_window_seconds`), and re-check. Success
   requires *growth*, or a live writable holder other than the proxy itself
   (`_log_has_live_writer`, already implemented).
2. **Container-aware resolution:** when `backend_rss.container_name(srv)` is
   set, resolve the backend's real output target via
   `podman exec <name> readlink /proc/<pid>/fd/1` (falling back to
   `/work/llama-server.log`, which the repo mount exposes at the project root),
   and watch that path instead of the unmounted host path.
3. **Fail loudly:** on failure log one ERROR naming the watched path, the
   resolved actual-writer path, the container name and the backend pid; set
   `llama_log_source_unhealthy=True` plus a new
   `llama_log_source_error` string; `/health` returns it. Never degrade to a
   silent "no samples".
4. Wire the check into startup after the backend is ready, and after adoption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A liveness check proves the proxy can read fresh llama-server output; a fixture where the log stops growing raises a visible error, and a test asserts the condition is not silently reported as "no samples".
- [ ] Container-backed deployments resolve the in-container log path and report it in the ERROR and in `/health`.
- [ ] A healthy (growing) log produces no new warning and leaves `llama_log_source_healthy` true.
- [ ] The check is bounded: it never blocks startup longer than the configured window and never restarts llama-server.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `ensure_log_liveness()` in `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` reusing
   `_resolve_llama_log_path`, `_log_has_live_writer`,
   `_resolve_live_backend_log_path`.

# Slot persistence: assert the path, suppress routine 501s

**Parent:** LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 · **Type:** feature · **Phase 6 of 8**

## Context

`server.session_slot_save_path` is `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache`, and
`start_llama_server()` exports it as `LLAMA_SLOT_SAVE_PATH`, which
`./start-llama.sh` turns into `--slot-save-path`. A launch outside the
lifecycle (the 2026-11-04 container) skipped that env var, so the server came up
without the flag and every `slot_save` returned 501 — fifteen times, each
swallowed at `debug` level (`proxy/proxy/router.py`). Decided behaviour:
**keep slot persistence enabled** and make a backend without the flag an
explicit, visible condition rather than a per-request warning.

## Change

1. At startup, assert `--slot-save-path` is present on the **live** backend
   (from `launch_authority` inspection, container-aware). Absent while
   `session_slot_save_path` is configured → log one WARNING naming the backend
   and the expected path, set `slot_persistence_disabled=True`, and never issue
   a save/restore call for that backend generation.
2. Leave persistence **enabled** when the flag matches the configured path
   (the decided behaviour, pinned by a test).
3. Treat a `501` from the slots endpoint as "server does not support slot
   actions": log exactly one WARNING with the remediation
   (`--slot-save-path` must be passed at launch), set
   `slot_persistence_disabled=True`, and skip further attempts. No 501 is ever
   logged as a routine per-request warning again.
4. Confirm every launch path forwards the env var — host (`./start-llama.sh`)
   and container (`./scripts/podman_start_llama.sh`, which already lists
   `LLAMA_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` in its forwarded set); add a test that the forwarded
   list still contains it so a future edit cannot silently drop it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `slot_save` either returns 200 (path configured) or is not attempted; a test pins whichever behaviour is chosen, and a 501 is never logged as a routine warning.
- [ ] A backend launched without `--slot-save-path` is detected at startup, reported once, and disables save/restore for that backend generation.
- [ ] The podman wrapper's forwarded env-var list is covered by a test asserting `LLAMA_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` is included.
- [ ] Slot save/restore continues to work unchanged when the flag is present (no regression in `proxy/tests/test_slot_save_eviction_timeout.py`).

## Minimal Implementation

1. `slot_persistence_enabled(srv, inspection) -> tuple[bool, str]` in
   `proxy/proxy/launch_authority.py` (or `proxy/proxy/session.py` if that is
   where the save path already gates — check before duplicating).
2. 501 handling in the slot-endpoint caller (`proxy/proxy/session.py` /
   `proxy/proxy/router.py`) with a module-level "unsupported" latch.
3. Early-return guards on the save and restore call sites.
4. Documentation note in `docs/dev/llama-launch-authority.md`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/launch_authority.py`
- `./scripts/podman_start_llama.sh`
- `./start-llama.sh`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_persistence_policy.py`

## Dependencies

Blocked by Phase 4 (tests) and Phase 2 (inspection module).

# 24 h report: name the log source instead of "no samples"

**Parent:** LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 · **Type:** feature · **Phase 7 of 8**

## Context

The 24 h proxy usage report has `## Decode speed`, `## Prompt eval speed` and
`## Engine cross-check` sections fed by
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/llama_log_parser.py`. On 2026-11-04
every llama-server file was `skipped_outside_window`, so the sections rendered
with no samples and no explanation — the eight-hour blind spot. The per-file
`FileDiagnostic.status` vocabulary exists (`STATUS_OUTSIDE_WINDOW`,
`STATUS_MISSING_PORT`, `STATUS_UNREADABLE`) but a *live-log-is-dead* condition
is not distinguishable from "the window simply contained no traffic".

## Change

1. Add a log-source diagnostic to the report: when the live `llama-server.log`
   is absent, stale beyond the configured window, or has no live writer, the
   three sections print a `log source unhealthy` block naming the resolved
   path (container-aware), its age, and the reason — with the same vocabulary
   used by `/health` (`llama_log_source_error`).
2. `llama_log_parser.iter_eval_timings` reports the reason as a distinct
   status (e.g. `skipped_log_source_dead`) so the sections can distinguish
   "no traffic in window" from "we could not read the engine log at all".
3. Report-side only: no change to how samples are aggregated when the source
   is healthy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The 24 h report's Decode speed / Prompt eval speed / Engine cross-check sections carry samples again, verified on a real run after the fix.
- [ ] When the engine log source is dead or stale, those sections state the log source, its resolved path and the reason instead of an unqualified "no samples".
- [ ] A healthy source is unchanged (no new noise in the section output) — pinned by a test.

## Goal

`discovered-from:LP-0MVWPK2VH008YWBD`

LP-0MVWPK2VH008YWBD landed the prefix-reuse and slot-steal counters (`llama_prefix_cache_reuse_total{outcome}`, `llama_slot_steal_total{reason}`) and committed the pre-registered decision threshold in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` (§"Prefix-reuse and slot-steal Prometheus series", commit 534e96d27). AC6 of that item requires the **verdict**, which needs a deployed measurement window; this item tracks producing it.

## Why it could not be closed on LP-0MVWPK2VH008YWBD

- The counters only exist from commit `534e96d27` on `dev`; they have not run for a full 24 h window.
- The shipped geometry is `session_slot_pool_size: 2` (`proxy/config.yaml`). The E7 mechanism (one slot, every session maps to slot 0, each switch evicts the previous prefix) is **not exercised** at two slots, so a two-slot window cannot demonstrate or refute it.

## What to do

1. Deploy the counters and capture at least one full 24 h window with a pool-of-one geometry (the single-slot A/B, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN, or a deliberate single-slot operating window).
2. Compute the pre-registered figures with the queries in REFERENCE.md:
   - reuse share = `sum(rate(llama_prefix_cache_reuse_total{outcome="reused"}[24h])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(llama_prefix_cache_reuse_total[24h])), 1)`
   - steal/evictions per 100 local turns = `100 * sum(increase(llama_slot_steal_total[24h])) / clamp_min(sum(increase(llama_prefix_cache_reuse_total[24h])), 1)`
   - size-filtered reuse (prompts > 20,000 tokens) from the nightly report per-dispatch `cached_ratio`.
3. Record the verdict as a comment on LP-0MVWPK2VH008YWBD (window boundaries, figures, exact query):
   - **steal real** (threshold (a) >= 5 steals/100 turns, or (b) reuse <= 50 % for >20k prompts across >=2 sessions in a pool of one) -> file a `discovered-from:LP-0MVWPK2VH008YWBD` follow-up naming the mechanism, the two metrics it moves with direction, effort band, and the pass/fail test.
   - **not demonstrated** -> state it with the figures and the failed threshold, and comment on LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ to downgrade/refute E7 (§5.8) rather than leave the 95 % steal claim standing.

The threshold may be tightened but **not loosened** after the fact.

## Finding

The proxy's log retention (7 days: `logging.retention_days` default in
`proxy/proxy/utils.py:1034`, which makes `TimedRotatingFileHandler` keep
`backupCount = 7 × 24 / 6 = 28` six-hour segments, with `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy`
as a `rotate 7` daily safety net) is shorter than the age a committed
measurement record reaches before it is audited or re-examined.

Concrete instance: `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` had to restate the pre-change baseline
on the window `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `2026-10-29 00:10:18` (8 days before the
implementing session). The window was measured in full on 2026-10-30, but by
2026-11-05 the first ~16 h of `2026-10-28` had been pruned: only
`proxy.log.2026-10-28_16.gz` (16:16:14→22:16:12) and
`proxy.log.2026-10-29_001015.gz` (00:00:00→00:10:15) survive — **6 h 10 m of a
24 h window (25.7 %, 67 of 136 enqueued waits)**. The committed record
therefore carries two provenance classes (measurement-time full window vs
today's coverage re-measurement) instead of a single regenerable artefact.

This is a recurring shape, not a one-off: any "measure a window, then commit a
record" slice that lands more than ~7 days after its window has to be
documented as un-reproducible, and every AC of the form "re-running the
embedded command regenerates the committed JSON" degrades to "regenerable
while the archives survive".

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want a measurement window to stay re-derivable for
at least as long as the records that quote it, so a committed record can be
re-checked by a later session instead of being taken on trust.

## Options (not a decision — intake should choose)

1. **Raise `logging.retention_days`** (e.g. 7→14 or 30). Cheap in disk: measured
   on 2026-11-05, `/var/log/llama-proxy` holds 46 `proxy.log*.gz` archives
   totalling **42 MB** (≈0.9 MB per six-hour segment), so doubling or
   quadrupling retention costs tens of MB, not GB. The knob already exists
   (`logging.retention_days`). Costs: more files in one directory (check
   `prune_logs` startup scan time) and the logrotate drop-in's `rotate 7`
   safety net must be raised to match, or it will prune what the in-process
   handler retains.
2. **Archive the window's archives with the record** — a `--emit-archives`
   mode or a documented `tar`/`rsync` step alongside a record commit. Larger
   repo footprint (or an external artefact store), but makes the record
   self-contained forever.
3. **Record the harness output as the artefact of authority** and drop the
   "regenerates byte-for-byte" expectation from records older than retention —
   documentation-only, no code change; what `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` does today.

## Acceptance criteria (draft, for intake)

- AC1: A documented retention window is at least as long as the longest-lived
  measurement record the project commits, with the value stated in
  `docs/dev/` and pinned by a test.
- AC2: A measurement record older than the retention window is either
  reproducible from a committed/archived artefact, or the record states its
  provenance classes explicitly (no silent re-derivation claim).
- AC3: Disk cost of the chosen retention is measured, not assumed, and stated
  on the host-install/retention doc.

## Evidence

- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-diurnal-baseline.md`
  ("Provenance and coverage") — the coverage map and the pruning mechanism.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` (`setup_logging`, `prune_logs`,
  `logging.retention_days` default 7).
- `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` (`rotate 7`, `size`-free daily safety net).
- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — rotation/decompression discovery (unaffected;
  the loss is retention, not discovery).
data.title: Proxy log retention (7 days) is shorter than the records that quote measured windows

discovered-from: LP-0MW3K7XJ30027RV6

## Observed (2026-11-05, while verifying the backend OOM ranking)

Starting the host-direct path (`./start-llama.sh router`, the `llama_allow_host_fallback` route) fails immediately:

```
$ /usr/local/bin/llama-server --version
/usr/local/bin/llama-server: error while loading shared libraries: libmtmd.so.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64 /usr/local/bin/llama-server --version
ggml_cuda_init: found 1 ROCm devices (Total VRAM: 122880 MiB)
version: 8782 (e97492369)
```

`/usr/local/lib64/libmtmd.so.0` exists, so the binary is fine — that directory is simply not on the loader path (no `ld.so.conf.d` entry) and `start-llama.sh` does not add it.

## Why it matters

`proxy/config.yaml` sets `llama_allow_host_fallback: true`, and host-first startup is attempted before the configured (podman) script. Today that attempt always fails and only logs a warning before falling back, so the host route is dead weight and a host-only deployment cannot start a backend at all. Latent, not urgent: the deployed path is the podman wrapper, which carries its own libraries.

## Suggested minimal fix

- Put `/usr/local/lib64` on the loader path in the install/refresh path (`ld.so.conf.d/llama.conf` + `ldconfig` from `install_proxy.sh`/`scripts/rebuild-llama.sh`), or export `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64` in `start-llama.sh` when the directory exists.
- Report a broken host binary at install time instead of only when the fallback is exercised.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `start-llama.sh <model>` starts the host `llama-server` without an externally supplied `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
- **AC2** — The install/rebuild path detects and reports a host binary that cannot load its libraries.
data.title: Host llama-server binary cannot start: libmtmd.so.0 not on the default library path

# Intake Brief: Improve the Web UI Prompt Log

## Headline

Make the `/logs` **Prompt Log** tab readable and more useful: show the *text* of the first message (not the dumped Python repr of its content-block list), and add a second **Current message** column showing the text of the request's last message.

## Problem statement

The Prompt Log tab records one entry per handled request and displays the request's first non-system message in a `Prompt (first non-system message)` column. For any client that sends structured content — which is *all* agent traffic, i.e. almost every entry — `proxy.prompt_log.extract_prompt()` reduces the message to `str(content)` of a content-block list, so the column renders a Python/JSON repr instead of prose:

```
[{'type': 'text', 'text': 'Do we have a work item that will improve logging in the web UI?'}]
```

Measured on the local `prompt-log.jsonl*` (≈114.5 K entries, 2026-11-17): **114 424** entries are repr'd block lists; only ~58 are plain text. The operator therefore has to decode a data structure to read a sentence — and the tab also only ever shows the *opening* prompt of a session, never what was actually just submitted.

## Users

**Primary:** the operator/LLM-proxy maintainer who uses the `/logs` page to audit and triage proxy traffic (which sessions are running, what they were asked, what was most recently asked).

**User stories:**

- "As an operator, I want the Prompt column to show the message *text*, so I can read what a session was asked without parsing a Python list."
- "As an operator, I want a second column with the message just submitted, so I can see the current turn of a long-running agent session rather than only its opening prompt."
- "As an operator, I want non-text payloads (images, tool results) marked explicitly instead of silently dropped, so I can tell a text-free request from an empty one — and I accept that entries recorded before this change keep their raw display rather than being rewritten."

## Existing state (verified in this checkout, `dev`)

- **Writer** — `proxy/proxy/prompt_log.py`: `record_exchange()` is hooked from `proxy.ui.proxy_openai_api`, resolves the session ID, requested model and routed model (`X-Resolved-Model` → `X-Provider` → `error:<code>`), and appends exactly one complete JSONL line per handled request. Bounded and non-fatal by contract: capped `prompt` (`prompt_log.max_prompt_chars`, default 2000, with a `truncated` flag), bounded tail read (`max_entries`, default 500), rotation to `prompt-log.jsonl.N` (`max_file_bytes`, `max_rotated_files`), daemon writer thread, counted `write_errors`/`dropped`, rate-limited error logging.
- **Extraction** — `extract_prompt()` returns `str(content)` via `router_helpers._first_message_content()` (first message whose `role != "system"`; `prompt` field for `/v1/completions`). `_first_message_content()` is **shared** with the `proxy.log` body preview (`_get_request_preview`, 80-char cap), so changing it in place would also change the existing log-preview behaviour.
- **Reader/API** — `recent_payload()` → `GET /logs/prompt-log` returns `{enabled, entries(newest-first), counters, max_entries, file}`; `recent_entries()` reads a bounded tail, newest first, and spans rotated files.
- **UI** — `proxy/templates/view_logs.html`: the Prompt Log tab (third tab, `switchTab('prompt')`) polls the endpoint every 5 s while visible and renders a table with columns **Time | Session | Routed model | Prompt (first non-system message)**; previews are capped at `PROMPT_PREVIEW_CHARS = 240` with a `…` marker and the full value in the `title` tooltip; all values pass through `escapeHtml()`.
- **Tests** — `proxy/tests/test_prompt_log.py` (25 tests: entry shape, session-ID chain, completions, routed-model resolution, truncation, disabled mode, append/rotation/read failures, config resolution/validation, endpoint shape, `/logs` page renders the tab). Playwright specs live alongside (`slot-logs.spec.js`, `status-bar.spec.js`, …).
- **Existing precedent** — `session_recorder._extract_message_text()` already flattens a content-block list into its `type: "text"` parts (used by the `/logs` session-dropdown preview, LP-0MRAZPRF6008537P) but it only handles the `text` type, only the first `role: "user"` message, and returns nothing for non-text blocks — it is a starting point to generalise rather than a drop-in.
- **Docs** — `proxy/README.md` § *Prompt Log (`prompt-log.jsonl`)* documents the field table and the tab; `README.md` line 45 summarises it.
- **Data reality** — of the repr'd entries sampled, 25 388 parse with `ast.literal_eval` (all `type: "text"` blocks) and 15 787 do **not** (truncated mid-block by `max_prompt_chars`). Recorded as evidence of the extent only: per D2, existing entries are **not** decoded or migrated — the fix applies to entries recorded from now on.

## Desired change

1. **First-message column shows text.** When a message's `content` is a list of content blocks, concatenate the `text` of its text parts (`type: "text"`, and `input_text` where present) instead of `str()`-ing the list. Plain-string content is unchanged.
2. **Second column: current message.** Add a `Current message` column showing the readable text of the request's **last non-system** message, labelled with that message's role, so an operator sees the turn in flight rather than only the session opener.
3. **Record the new field** in the JSONL (so the file itself stays the source of truth and stays greppable), keeping the existing `prompt` field's meaning intact for backwards compatibility.
4. **Entries already on disk are left alone.** No read-time decoding, no repr parsing and no file migration: the tab becomes readable for entries recorded after this change, while older rows keep today's raw display until they age out of the window/rotation.

## Implementation plan (ordered; test-first where practical)

1. **Test-first: pure helpers in `proxy/proxy/prompt_log.py`.** Write the failing tests in `proxy/tests/test_prompt_log.py` for two new helpers — `flatten_message_content(content)` (a string passes through unchanged; a block list concatenates its `text`/`input_text` parts; each non-text block becomes a short placeholder such as `<image>` / `<tool_result:1234 chars>`; empty/no-text content yields a single placeholder or `""` as specified) and `extract_last_non_system_message(body_json)` returning `(text, role)` while skipping any `role == "system"`. Then implement them.
   Verify: `pytest proxy/tests/test_prompt_log.py -k "flatten or last_message"` green; `ruff check` clean.
2. **Wire the writer.** Switch `extract_prompt()` to the flattener (**leave `router_helpers._first_message_content()` untouched** — it also feeds the `proxy.log` body preview) and add `current_prompt`, `current_prompt_role`, `current_prompt_truncated` to `build_entry()`/`record_exchange()`, each capped by `prompt_log.max_prompt_chars`.
   Verify: the existing writer/queue/rotation tests still pass; new tests assert the added fields, the caps and that recording stays non-blocking and non-fatal.
3. **Pin the read path.** No change to `recent_entries()`/`recent_payload()`: add a regression test asserting a stored legacy repr-style entry passes through the endpoint byte-for-byte unchanged (raw display, as today).
4. **UI.** In `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` add the `Current message` column immediately after the first-message column (role label + `PROMPT_PREVIEW_CHARS` cap + full text in `title`, both via `escapeHtml`), reusing the existing preview/tooltip convention.
   Verify: an endpoint/page test asserts the new `<th>`; a rendering assertion shows no `{'type':` fragment for a new-style entry and a placeholder for a non-text block.
5. **Docs.** `proxy/README.md` § *Prompt Log (`prompt-log.jsonl`)*: new fields in the table, the text-extraction rule, the second column, and the explicit "readable only for entries recorded after this change" limitation; `README.md` prompt-log bullet.
6. **Gate.** Full suite via `/skill:test`, then commit in build → test → commit order and stage the item `in_review`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For a request whose first non-system message content is a content-block list (e.g. `[{"type":"text","text":"…"}]`), `GET /logs/prompt-log` returns prose text for the first-message field — never a Python/JSON repr — and the `/logs` Prompt Log table shows no `{'type':` fragment for any entry recorded after this change. Verified by a pytest test on the payload plus a UI assertion.
- [ ] The Prompt Log table has a second `Current message` column rendering the readable text of the request's **last non-system** message, labelled with that message's role, with the same preview cap and hover-full-text behaviour as the first-message column.
- [ ] New JSONL entries carry both prompts (existing `prompt` field semantics unchanged; new field(s) for the current message plus its role and truncation flag), each capped by `prompt_log.max_prompt_chars`; recording remains non-blocking, bounded and never fatal (existing writer contract and its tests unchanged).
- [ ] Non-text content blocks (image, tool result, etc.) are rendered as short placeholders (e.g. `<image>`, `<tool_result:1234 chars>`) rather than dropped silently or dumped raw; a message with no text blocks renders exactly one placeholder. A trailing `role: "system"` message is never selected or displayed.
- [ ] The read path is unchanged in cost and shape: no repr/JSON decoding of stored entries, no additional file reads, and the existing bounded window (`max_entries`) is preserved — asserted by a test that a legacy repr-style entry still round-trips through the endpoint unchanged (it renders raw, exactly as today).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`README.md` prompt-log bullet and `proxy/README.md` § *Prompt Log*: field table gains the new fields, the tab description gains the second column and the text-extraction rule, and the "readable only for new entries" limitation is stated).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (via the test skill / `run_tests.py`), with `ruff` clean on changed files.

## Impact

Operators can read at a glance what each proxy request actually asked — both the session's opening prompt and the message just submitted — instead of decoding a dumped Python data structure.

## Constraints

- Implement in this repo (`llm-manager`, FastAPI app under `proxy/`), on `dev`; pushes only to `dev` (release promotes `dev` → `main`).
- **Do not change the shared `router_helpers._first_message_content()` behaviour** — it also feeds the `proxy.log` body preview (80-char cap, different redaction/display contract). Flattening belongs in the prompt-log path (a prompt-log-scoped helper, or a flatten step applied in `prompt_log.py`).
- System-prompt content must stay out of the log and the UI — the "first non-system message" and last-message rules must never surface a `role: "system"` message. If the *last* message is a system message (rare, e.g. a trailing steering message), it must be skipped rather than displayed.
- Preserve the writer's existing contract: one complete line written once, bounded queue, bounded file growth, bounded tail reads, append failures counted and never raised into the request path.
- No schema-breaking change: old entries must keep working with the new reader (field-by-field, tolerant of missing new fields), and old readers are not a concern (single deployable).
- **Legacy entries are out of scope (operator decision, D2).** Do not add read-time repr/JSON decoding of stored `prompt` values, and do not rewrite `prompt-log.jsonl*`. Older rows may keep showing the raw repr until they age out — that is accepted.
- Follow existing Web UI conventions in `view_logs.html` (CSS variables, `escapeHtml`, table classes `.prompt-log-table`, preview constants).
- Out of scope: new prompt-log features beyond these two columns (search/filter, export, token counts, embeddings/TTS recording, retention changes).

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Cost on the read/write path.** Flattening happens once per request at record time and per rendered entry at read time, inside the existing bounded window (`max_entries`, default 500); no whole-file work and no extra file reads. Prompts are already capped at 2000 chars.
- **R2 — "Last non-system message" is often a tool result in agent traffic.** The column may frequently show tool output rather than a fresh user instruction; the role label makes that explicit and is the agreed presentation (D1).
- **R3 — Mixed readability during transition.** Entries written before this change keep the repr display (D2: only new entries are fixed), so the tab will show both styles side by side until old entries age out of the 500-entry window / rotation. Accepted; documented in `proxy/README.md`.
- **R4 — Duplicate/coalesced requests** keep producing one entry each (existing contract); both entries will carry the same current-message text.
- **R5 — Scope creep.** Search/filtering, column sorting, legacy back-fill and prompt-log retention changes are neighbouring ideas — record them as linked work items rather than absorbing them here (`LP-0MW3GU0JO008XOUF` already covers retention).
- **A1 —** "Content of the current message" means the request's last **non-system** message in the payload, not the proxy's *response* (operator answer, D1).
- **A2 —** The UI keeps its current 240-char preview + tooltip convention for both columns rather than introducing full-text expansion.
- **A3 —** Non-text blocks are represented by placeholders; a message with only non-text blocks shows placeholders only (operator answer, D3).

## Decisions recorded during intake

- **D1 — "The current message" = the last non-system message in the request payload, labelled with its role.** Operator answer (2026-11-17), interactive intake round. Rejected: last message regardless of role (can surface a trailing system/steering message); last `role: "user"` only (hides tool-result turns).
- **D2 — Only new entries get readable text; legacy entries are not decoded.** Operator answer (2026-11-17). Rejected: read-time decoding of stored repr strings (measured feasible — 100 % of the 15 787 truncated entries remained parseable — but not wanted); rewriting the existing file.
- **D3 — Non-text content blocks render as short placeholders** (`<image>`, `<tool_result:1234 chars>`). Operator answer (2026-11-17). Rejected: dropping them silently; dumping them raw.
- **D4 — The current-message column is additive** and sits immediately after the first-message column. Source: the item description ("Add a second column that adds the content of the current message").

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prompt_log.py` — add a content-block text flattener (text parts concatenated, non-text parts as placeholders), a last-non-system-message extractor, and the new entry fields. **No** changes to legacy decode behaviour in `recent_entries`/`recent_payload`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — reuse `_first_message_content()`'s message-selection policy; **read-only** for this change (shared with the `proxy.log` body preview).
- `proxy/proxy/session_recorder.py` — **reuse candidate**: `_extract_message_text()` already flattens `type: "text"` content parts for the session-dropdown preview; generalise it (or share a helper with it) rather than duplicating the logic.
- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — add the `Current message` column, render both previews as text, keep `PROMPT_PREVIEW_CHARS`/tooltip/`escapeHtml` conventions and the `.prompt-log-table` styles.
- `proxy/tests/test_prompt_log.py` — unit tests: flattener (string / one block / many blocks / mixed blocks / empty), last-non-system-message selection (incl. trailing system message skipped), entry shape and caps, endpoint payload, a legacy repr entry passing through unchanged, and a `/logs` page assertion for the new column.
- `proxy/README.md` — § *Prompt Log (`prompt-log.jsonl`)*: new fields in the table, the text-extraction rule, the second column.
- `README.md` — the prompt-log bullet in the Web UI feature list.

## Related work

- **Prompt log: track the first message of each proxy request (time, prompt, session ID, routed model) in a log, with a Web UI tab (LP-0MVP79OBP002G6Z1)** — completed; built the log, the endpoint and the tab this item improves.
- **Rethink logs display: remove model tabs, flat session list with message previews (LP-0MRAG775K008CKDG)** — completed; the earlier readability pass on the same page.
- **Web UI logs interface that shows the current logs for each active slot (LP-0MSHET5SI000LYSK)** — completed; established the tabbed `/logs` layout (and `slot_log_filter.py`, the closest existing example of a pure, unit-tested log-projection helper).
- **Add user message preview (first 80 chars) to session dropdown entries (LP-0MRAZPRF6008537P)** — completed; the closest precedent for rendering request text in this UI (`session_recorder._extract_message_text` + `_truncate_preview`).
- **Proxy log retention (7 days) is shorter than the records that quote measured windows (LP-0MW3GU0JO008XOUF)** — open; the retention counterpart, explicitly out of scope here.
- **Web UI to log input and output tokens (LP-0MV592AU008VAP4)** — open; adjacent UI work on the same page, not overlapping.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is 'the current message' in the second column — the last message regardless of role, the last non-system message, or the last `role: user` message?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-17): "last non-system message". Source: interactive intake reply. Recorded as D1.
- Q: "Should old entries (already written as repr'd block lists) be decoded at read time as well, or only new entries fixed?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-17): "Only new entries". Source: interactive intake reply. Recorded as D2; supersedes the draft's recommended read-time decoding, and the corresponding AC/constraint/risk entries were updated.
- Q: "How should non-text content blocks appear — placeholder, dropped, or raw?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-17): "short placeholders". Source: interactive intake reply. Recorded as D3.
- Q: "Is the current-message column additive (second column) and placed after the first-message column?" — Answer (operator, item description): "Add a second column that adds the content of the current message." Source: work-item description `LP-0MW5M3C0A008QPVP`. Recorded as D4.
## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-17 — plan skill (auto-complete, effort Small / risk Low):** pre-check returned `skip` (Small + Low) — no child decomposition. Six review stages run on the existing brief:
  - *Requirements & AC alignment:* replaced the third user story, which still asked for legacy-entry recovery — contradicted by the operator decision D2 — with a story aligned to D3 (explicit placeholders) plus the accepted legacy limitation. Normalised cross-references from OQ1–OQ3 to D1–D3.
  - *Completeness / Key Files:* `validate_key_files_format()` clean (6 paths, all with directory + extension); every AC has a matching requirement or decision.
  - *Sequencing & dependencies:* no children (single deliverable slice); the ordered implementation plan embeds test-first ordering (tests for the helpers land before the writer/UI wiring).
  - *Scope sizing:* kept as one Small item — splitting would create sub-hour children; the six ordered steps are the implementation increments.
  - *Acceptance & testability:* all 7 ACs are pass/fail with named verification (pytest assertions, endpoint payload, docs, full suite); AC5 pins "no legacy decoding" as a positive regression assertion.
  - *Polish & handoff:* added `## Implementation plan (ordered; test-first where practical)`; effort/risk re-confirmed (Small, 17.5h recommended, Low risk 2/25).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRAZPRF6008537P** – Add user message preview (first 80 chars) to session dropdown entries (completed)
- **LP-0MUIEK483002TZ54** – Add shared proxy log discovery + gzip-open helper (completed)
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, active, actually, add (+446 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, active, actually, add (+446 more)

## Goal

Produce a **proposal** (no implementation without explicit producer approval) for separating audit/bulk traffic from interactive user traffic at the shared local gate.

**Discovered from:** LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I. Rec 5 of the root-cause analysis. **This item must not change code, config or the running proxy.**

## Why it matters (measured, certified window 2026-11-06 14:15:50 → 2026-11-08 00:00)

- **20 of the 60** `prefill_deadline` events are audit sessions (`audit-*`), with 44k–103k prompts; 11 audit events are attributed capacity and 9 predicted-warmth.
- Audit is excluded from the (b2) user-class criterion, **but not from its cause**: audit prefills occupy the shared gate and the second slot, and the measured cold rate swings **235–295 tok/s (contended) vs 530–770 tok/s (best case)**.
- Audits raise the occupancy class (9/60, 15 %, and under-counted while `/slots` times out), i.e. they make *user* events miss even though their own events are not counted.

## Scope

**In:** a written proposal in `docs/dev/` (or an appendix to the existing prefill/admission docs) covering options, costs and the decision criteria.

**Out:** any implementation, config change, deployment or proxy restart. Implementation happens only in a follow-up item created **after** producer approval.

## Options the proposal must cost

1. **Audit remote-only** (or audit-on-a-different-provider): zero local audit load; cost = remote tokens/latency.
2. **Idle-gated local access for audits**: local only when the pool has been idle ≥ N s; needs a measured N.
3. **Priority-weighted gate**: user `high`/`medium` pre-empts queued audit prefills; needs the priority plumbing already present (LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI).
4. **Per-class deadline**: audits get a shorter local deadline (e.g. 60 s) and fall back sooner.
5. **Do nothing** — with the measured cost stated.

For each: expected effect on the user-class rate, on local coverage/utilisation, on remote spend, and the risk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Proposal written.** A document states each option, its mechanism, the measured evidence it rests on, expected effect on the user-class combined rate (baseline 2.223/h; target ≤ 0.5/h), local coverage, and remote cost. It names a recommendation and the decision criteria.
- **AC2 — No implementation.** The item changes **no** source, config or runtime state; git diff is empty apart from the proposal document (or the doc lives in the work item description if a doc is premature). No proxy restart is performed by this item.
- **AC3 — Impact model reproducible.** The projected numbers come from a stated, reproducible computation over the certified window dataset (`/tmp/ac3-window-2026-11-06.json`, recorded on LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) — e.g. "remove audit events → X user events remain, Y/h", with the command/analysis recorded.
- **AC4 — Producer approval gate.** `needsProducerReview` is set on creation; the item advances only when the producer records approval (a comment naming the chosen option). Until then it stays `idea`/`intake_complete` and dispatchable-for-proposal only.
- **AC5 — Follow-up on approval.** On approval, create the implementation item (issue type `feature`, high) carrying: the restart AC (proxy restarted via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` with PID/HEAD/`/health` evidence), the dated-title re-anchor AC, and the impact measurement. Link it here with `related`/`depends-on` as appropriate.
- **AC6 — Proxy restart AC (deferred, not waived).** This item performs no restart. The restart it is accountable for is the one in the approved follow-up: that follow-up must restart the proxy and record old/new PID, start time, deployed HEAD and `/health` before its impact measurement. If the producer rejects the proposal, state explicitly that no restart is owed and close.
- **AC7 — Dated titles.** The dated-title re-anchor (`\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` in open titles) is owed by the approved follow-up's restart; this item records that obligation and, on rejection, notes that no re-anchor is triggered.

## Relationship

- Related: LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (serialise audits at the shared local resource), LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI (batch work must send a priority header so interactive sessions are protected), LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 (early-released local dispatch starvation).
- The producer's (b2) re-scope conversation (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) should consider this proposal as one of the levers.

## Earliest date/time for implementation

**2026-11-07T14:16Z** — the measurement window anchor plus 24 h.

Per the shared convention in [`docs/dev/measurement-windows.md`](docs/dev/measurement-windows.md) (LP-0MVWC0FAT0018PMW):

- **Window anchor** = the proxy restart that loaded the rung. That is the running process

  `local_last_resort*` symbols; the rung had merged to `dev` as `52130e54d` on 2026-11-05 05:48, ~32 h earlier.
- **Window start** = the first whole minute after that restart → **2026-11-06T14:16Z**.
- **Earliest the window can close** = window start + 24 h → **2026-11-07T14:16Z**.

That instant has passed (the same anchor already serves LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K, LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8 and
LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q, all of which quote `2026-11-06T14:16Z → 2026-11-07T14:16Z`), so this item is actionable
immediately — the date above is a floor, not a start signal.

Two further constraints:

- **The window must be restart-free.** A restart inside it (`start-proxy.sh --restart`, a deploy, a crash
  recovery) re-anchors it: a partial window never yields a PASS. Confirm with `ps -o lstart` on the uvicorn pid
  and by grepping the window's logs for `Starting LLama Proxy Server`. Coordinate with the shared calendar
  before any deploy.
- **Act before ≈ 2026-11-13.** `logging.retention_days` is 7 (`proxy/config.yaml`), so the post-deploy segments
  (`proxy.log.2026-11-07_*`, `proxy.log.2026-11-08_*`) are pruned roughly 7 days after the deploy. Past that
  the window must be re-based on a fresh deploy (`docs/dev/proxy-usage-evidence-windows.md` covers archiving
  the raw segments first).

## Goal

As the proxy operator, I want the ≥ 24 h post-deploy evaluation of the last-resort local admission rung (AC8 of LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W) performed and recorded, so that the rung is either confirmed to reduce `All providers exhausted` failures inside idle gaps without a regression in prefill evictions/discarded tokens, or is killed/retuned with the measured evidence.

## Why this is a separate item

AC8 of LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W is a *post-deploy* criterion: it cannot be satisfied by code, tests or documentation, only by a measurement window taken after the rung has been running in production. The implementation item delivered the rung, the tests and the measurement surfaces (`docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` → "Last-resort rung (LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W): the post-deploy measurement"); the actual window belongs here.

Baseline to beat (measured 2026-10-29 23:43:30 → 2026-10-30 23:43:30, *before* the rung existed):

- 236 of the window's 686 `All providers exhausted` warnings (34%) occurred inside 13 GPU-idle gaps carrying 98 inbound requests and 0 streams.
- The idle-admit ladder fired 1,337 times and refused 1,291 (96.6%) on `prefill_budget_exceeded`; 292,924 prefill tokens / 44 evictions discarded per 24 h.

## In scope

- Run the usage analysis over a ≥ 24 h window that lies entirely after the deployment instant, e.g.
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-11-06 14:16:00" --end "2026-11-07 14:16:00"` (the CLI supports arbitrary `--start`/`--end`), and repeat for a later restart-free window if the first is inconclusive.
- Attribute every `local_last_resort_admit` line (`estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `idle_seconds`, `threshold_seconds`, `deadline_s`, `warm_cap`, `remote_exhausted=true`, `session`, `turn`) and every `routing_idle_admit_refused` it superseded.
- Read the three comparison surfaces from the same window: `All providers exhausted` inside idle gaps vs the 236 baseline, `local_evictions_after_acceptance` with `reason=prefill_deadline`, and discarded prefill tokens.
- Record the numbers, the window boundaries, the exact commands and the verdict on this item, and bring the result back to LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W (comment, and re-audit that item so its AC8 — now scoped to this handover — stays consistent with the measured outcome).

## Out of scope

- Any code change. If the evaluation shows `local_last_resort_deadline_seconds` too low (rising `prefill_deadline` evictions), the fix is a raised knob value, filed as its own item; if it shows no benefit, the fix is the kill switch (`local_last_resort_idle_seconds: 0`), also its own item.
- Re-measuring remote provider quota/capacity root causes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A restart-free ≥ 24 h window lying entirely after the window start (2026-11-06T14:16Z) is analysed with the deterministic CLI, and the window boundaries, the restart-free evidence (`ps -o lstart` on the uvicorn pid, no `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker inside the window) and the exact command are recorded on this item.
- AC2: The window's `All providers exhausted` count inside GPU-idle gaps is reported against the 236/686 baseline, with the idle-gap definition and the gap count stated.
- AC3: `local_last_resort_admit` lines in the window are counted and attributed (per-session/per-turn) with their `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `idle_seconds`, `deadline_s` distribution; if the count is zero, the reason is stated (remote chain never empty, prompt above warm cap, or GPU not idle) with the supporting log evidence.
- AC4: `local_evictions_after_acceptance` (`reason=prefill_deadline`) and discarded prefill tokens are reported for the window and compared with the pre-rung 24 h figures (44 evictions / 292,924 discarded prefill tokens).
- AC5: An explicit verdict — **keep** (exhaustions inside idle gaps fell, neither eviction metric rose), **retune** (`local_last_resort_deadline_seconds` too low — quote the distribution) or **kill** (`local_last_resort_idle_seconds: 0`) — recorded on this item with the numbers that justify it, and echoed as a comment on LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W.
- AC6: If the window is inconclusive (no remote-exhaustion episode coincided with an idle GPU), that is recorded explicitly with the evidence and the item stays open for a later ≥ 24 h window — an inconclusive window is never reported as a pass.

## Measurement surfaces

Documented in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` (section "Last-resort rung (LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W): the post-deploy measurement"): `local_last_resort_admit` grep count, `All providers exhausted` inside idle gaps, usage-report `local_evictions_after_acceptance`, and the prefill-token accounting. Knobs and rationale: `proxy/config.yaml` (`local_last_resort_idle_seconds: 300`, `local_last_resort_deadline_seconds: 600`), `proxy/docs/routing.md` → "Last-resort local admission".

## Problem
Running `wl doctor upgrade` rewrites the committed `.githooks/pre-push`, `.githooks/post-merge` and `.githooks/post-rewrite` from this repo's committed v4/v2 templates to the ContextHub wl CLI's canonical v3/v1 templates (`PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`). This is a silent DOWNGRADE: the committed v4 pre-push hook has the pushed-commit guard and emits 'ERROR: no test runner found — ...', which `tests/test_git_hooks.py:428` asserts; the CLI v3 hook emits 'ERROR: run_tests.py not found — ...' and lacks the guard. The downgrade turns the working tree red and would also be a regression if committed.

## Impact
- Discovered while auditing LP-0MW305AJ80085AEK: `wl doctor upgrade` (run to clear a schemaVersion error) left the three hooks dirty, so the full suite failed on `tests/test_git_hooks.py::test_missing_runner_fails_closed_on_dev_push` and the audit's F3 triage created a false-positive test-failure item (LP-0MWC0K2DD0073YML, since closed).
- Any dev push from the dirty checkout would trip the repo's own pushed-commit dirty-tree guard.

## Evidence
- `git diff` on the three hook files reverts committed v4/v2 to the CLI v3/v1 content; the CLI text carries RISE-0MVSS1KVV002TJUL.
- CLI source: /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/dist/doctor/hook-upgrade.js (`PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`) and dist/commands/doctor/upgrade.js (invokes `upgradeHooks('.githooks', ...)`).
- Fix applied locally: `git checkout -- .githooks/pre-push .githooks/post-merge .githooks/post-rewrite`.

## Desired behaviour
`wl doctor upgrade` must not overwrite a project hook that has evolved beyond the CLI template (or must detect the newer version and no-op), so it can never silently downgrade committed hooks.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `wl doctor upgrade` leaves an already-newer committed hook untouched (no-op), verified by a test.
2. `wl doctor upgrade` does not modify `.githooks/` files whose committed content differs from the CLI template in a way the CLI cannot prove is older.
3. Full project test suite passes with the change.

# Grant `tailscale serve` privileges so Grafana is reachable on the tailnet

## Why

`scripts/deploy_grafana.sh` publishes Grafana on the tailnet with
`tailscale serve --bg --tcp=3000`. On this host that call is refused:

```
sending serve config: Access denied: serve config denied
Use 'sudo tailscale set --operator=rgardler'.
```

`tailscaled` only accepts serve configuration from root or from the configured
**operator**. The agent runs as `rgardler`, there is no passwordless sudo, and
`tailscale serve status` reports `No serve config`. The script therefore
degrades to loopback-only with a warning — the behaviour the parent epic's
AC 4 explicitly specifies — and the dashboard is reachable at
`http://127.0.0.1:3000` but not at `http://100.79.231.101:3000`.

## What is needed (operator action — requires sudo)

Run **one** of:

```
sudo tailscale set --operator=rgardler     # preferred: no root needed afterwards
```

or make the serve call itself privileged, then:

```
tailscale serve --bg --tcp=3000 http://127.0.0.1:3000
tailscale serve status                      # expect a :3000 TCP forwarder
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://100.79.231.101:3000/api/health
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. `sudo tailscale set --operator=rgardler` has been run (or serve config is otherwise permitted for `rgardler`), so `tailscale serve --bg --tcp=3000 http://127.0.0.1:3000` succeeds without sudo.
2. `tailscale serve status` shows a `:3000` TCP forwarder to `http://127.0.0.1:3000`.
3. `http://100.79.231.101:3000/api/health` reports `"database": "ok"` from the tailnet address.
4. `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh` re-run reports `published on the tailnet via tailscale serve --tcp=3000` (no degradation warning) and `--check` still exits `0`.
5. `ss -tln` still shows Grafana bound to `127.0.0.1:3000` only — the tailnet path is Tailscale's listener, not a widened bind.

## Notes

- This item is operator-gated: an agent cannot supply the sudo password. It is
  not a code defect — the script already implements the documented degradation
  path correctly.
- No secret is involved: the admin password stays in
  `~/.config/grafana/admin.pass` (`0600`).

## Impact

Once the serve privilege is granted, the memory dashboard is reachable from any
device on the tailnet instead of only from this host's loopback.


## Origin

Discovered during work on LP-0MWCQKN3C0034R6Z (epic LP-0MVWUTC2J006PKBJ). Not a blocker: the epic's AC 4 explicitly specifies loopback-only degradation when `tailscale serve` is unavailable, and it is unavailable to this non-privileged account. This item records the privileged step needed to *also* expose the dashboard on the tailnet.

discovered-from:LP-0MWCQKN3C0034R6Z
data.title: Grant tailscale serve privileges so the Grafana dashboard is reachable on the tailnet
